narr: A deep southerly fetch of rich moisture up from the Gulf of California led to scattered to widespread heavy rainfall in portions of Southwest Arizona during the afternoon of the 1st. Moisture values were well above normal for the time of year with precipitable water values analyzed around 2.0-2.2 inches. Favorable dynamic and orographic forcing helped lead to strong updrafts and training of storms over certain terrain areas. Radar estimated rain rates were up to around 2-3 inches per hour with locally higher rates over shorter periods. These high rain rates led to areas of high rainfall accumulation, with some areas of more than 1 inch of rain and isolated areas up to 2.5-3.5 inches, radar estimated. Highest measured rainfall were between 1.5-2.0 inches. This resulted in multiple reports of flash flooding in the region, including flooding of the Gila River in Yuma County. On top of the flooding, the heavy mass loading, strong updrafts, and strong cold pools resulted in strong to severe outflow winds emanating out from the showers and storms. , which led to a few severe wind reports and generated dust storm conditions in some areas.
ev: Report of flooding on Highway 95 near mile post 59. Timing based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Video evidence showed considerable flow from the Gila River that resulted in erosion along Mohawk Valley Road, located approximately 5 miles west-northwest of Tacna. Timing estimated from radar. A USGS gauge on the Gila River near Dome/Yuma, roughly 25 miles downstream, recorded a rapid 4-foot rise later in the evening. No injuries were reported.
Rural road between County 2nd St and County 3rd St near Tacna closed due to significant flow from Gila River. Timing estimated based on radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Significant water flow across the Martinez Lake area, resulting in road damage. Timing based on radar. No injuries were reported.
